{{Short description|Statistical method in hydrology}}
'''Generalized [[likelihood]] [[uncertainty]] [[estimation]]''' ('''GLUE''') is a statistical method used in [[hydrology]] for quantifying the uncertainty of model predictions. The method was introduced by [[Keith Beven]] and Andrew Binley in 1992.<ref name="BevenBinley1992">{{cite journal|last1=Beven|first1=Keith|last2=Binley|first2=Andrew|title=The future of distributed models: Model calibration and uncertainty prediction|journal=Hydrological Processes|volume=6|issue=3|year=1992|pages=279–298|issn=0885-6087|doi=10.1002/hyp.3360060305|bibcode=1992HyPr....6..279B }}</ref><ref name="BevenBinley2014">{{cite journal|last1=Beven|first1=Keith|last2=Binley|first2=Andrew|title=GLUE: 20 years on|journal=Hydrological Processes|volume=28|issue=24|year=2014|pages=5897–5918|issn=0885-6087|doi=10.1002/hyp.10082|doi-access=free|bibcode=2014HyPr...28.5897B |url=http://uu.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:689297/FULLTEXT01}}</ref> The basic idea of GLUE is that given our inability to represent exactly in a [[mathematical model]] how nature works, there will always be several different models that mimic equally well an observed natural process (such as [[discharge (hydrology)|river discharge]]). Such equally acceptable or [[behavioral]] models are therefore called [[equifinality|equifinal]].<ref name="BevenFreer2001">{{cite journal|last1=Beven|first1=Keith|last2=Freer|first2=Jim|title=Equifinality, data assimilation, and uncertainty estimation in mechanistic modelling of complex environmental systems using the GLUE methodology|journal=Journal of Hydrology|volume=249|issue=1–4|year=2001|pages=11–29|issn=0022-1694|doi=10.1016/S0022-1694(01)00421-8|bibcode=2001JHyd..249...11B }}</ref>

The methodology deals with models whose results are expressed as [[probability distribution]]s of possible outcomes, often in the form of [[Monte Carlo simulation]]s, and the problem can be viewed as assessing, and comparing between models, how good these representations of uncertainty are. There is an implicit understanding that the models being used are approximations to what might be obtained from a thorough [[Bayesian analysis]] of the problem if a fully adequate model of real-world hydrological processes were available.<ref>Beven, K.J., 2007: [http://www.hydrol-earth-syst-sci.net/11/460/2007/hess-11-460-2007.pdf Towards integrated environmental models of everywhere: uncertainty, data and modelling as a learning process.] [[Hydrology and Earth System Sciences]], 11(1), p. 460–467.</ref><ref name="MantovanTodini2006">{{cite journal|last1=Mantovan|first1=Pietro|last2=Todini|first2=Ezio|title=Hydrological forecasting uncertainty assessment: Incoherence of the GLUE methodology|journal=Journal of Hydrology|volume=330|issue=1–2|year=2006|pages=368–381|issn=0022-1694|doi=10.1016/j.jhydrol.2006.04.046|bibcode=2006JHyd..330..368M }}</ref>
<ref name="BevenSmith2007">{{cite journal|last1=Beven|first1=Keith|last2=Smith|first2=Paul|last3=Freer|first3=Jim|title=Comment on "Hydrological forecasting uncertainty assessment: Incoherence of the GLUE methodology" by Pietro Mantovan and Ezio Todini|journal=Journal of Hydrology|volume=338|issue=3–4|year=2007|pages=315–318|issn=0022-1694|doi=10.1016/j.jhydrol.2007.02.023|bibcode=2007JHyd..338..315B }}</ref>
<ref name="StedingerVogel2008">{{cite journal|last1=Stedinger|first1=Jery R.|last2=Vogel|first2=Richard M.|last3=Lee|first3=Seung Uk|last4=Batchelder|first4=Rebecca|title=Appraisal of the generalized likelihood uncertainty estimation (GLUE) method|journal=Water Resources Research|volume=44|issue=12|year=2008|issn=0043-1397|doi=10.1029/2008WR006822|doi-access=free|bibcode=2008WRR....44.0B06S }}</ref>

GLUE is equivalent to [[Approximate Bayesian computation]] for some choices of summary statistic and threshold.<ref name="sadegh_vrugt_2013">{{cite journal |last1=Sadegh |first1=M. |last2=Vrugt |first2=J. A. |title=Bridging the gap between GLUE and formal statistical approaches: approximate Bayesian computation |journal=Hydrology and Earth System Sciences |date=2013 |volume=17 |issue=12 |pages=4831–4850 |doi=10.5194/hess-17-4831-2013|doi-access=free |bibcode=2013HESS...17.4831S }}</ref><ref name="nott_2012">{{cite journal |last1=Nott |first1=David J. |last2=Marshall |first2=Lucy |last3=Brown |first3=Jason |title=Generalized likelihood uncertainty estimation (GLUE) and approximate Bayesian computation: What's the connection? |journal=Water Resources Research |date=2012 |volume=48 |issue=12 |doi=10.1029/2011WR011128|doi-access=free |bibcode=2012WRR....4812602N }}</ref>
